title: Why .gitignore won't ignore app.log
hook: IT'S IN .GITIGNORE. GIT STILL TRACKS IT.
question: Tracked by mistake: log files or node_modules?
fact_source: https://git-scm.com/docs/gitignore (Files already tracked by Git are not affected; to stop tracking a file that is currently tracked, use git rm --cached) + https://git-scm.com/docs/git-rm (--cached: remove paths only from the index, working tree files left alone)

scenes.headline: Git still tracks app.log
scenes.sub: app.log is in .gitignore. git status: modified.
scenes.voice: You added app dot log to git ignore, but git still shows it as modified?
scenes.caption: You added app.log to .gitignore, but Git still shows it as modified?

scenes.headline: .gitignore skips tracked files
scenes.voice: Git ignore only works on untracked files. Files already tracked by git are not affected.
scenes.caption: .gitignore only works on untracked files. Files already tracked by Git are not affected.

scenes.headline: Untrack it with --cached
scenes.voice: Run git r m, dash dash cached, app dot log, then commit. Your file stays on disk.
scenes.caption: Run git rm --cached app.log, then commit. Your file stays on disk.

scenes.headline: Now .gitignore works
scenes.voice: Now the file is untracked, so git ignore keeps it out of later commits.
scenes.caption: Now the file is untracked, so .gitignore keeps it out of later commits.

scenes.voice: What did you track by mistake: log files or node modules? Comment your answer.
scenes.caption: What did you track by mistake: log files or node_modules? Comment your answer.
